name: Animated Bar Chart Wipe
use_when: A documentary explainer needs a simple statistic, comparison, trend, or rank visualized quickly.
The data can be understood as a small bar chart without requiring a full data-viz system.
The chart should share the same editorial paper/serif style as the rest of the sequence.
avoid_when: The data source is unknown, unverified, or too complex for a simple chart.
The chart lacks labels or scale context needed to avoid misleading viewers.
The animation would make bars feel more precise than the source data supports.

timeline_pattern.pattern: chart_background -> x_axis_y_axis -> axis_labels -> bar_shapes_or_text_underscores -> directional_wipe_in -> stagger_bars -> compound_clip -> slide_or_fade_out
timeline_pattern.data_rule: Know the value each bar represents before animating.
timeline_pattern.axis_rule: Axis labels must be readable or intentionally omitted only when context already makes the chart clear.
timeline_pattern.stagger_rule: Bars can stagger to guide comparison order, but should not distort data meaning.

motion.rule: Bars should grow in the value direction and settle before the viewer needs to compare them.

keyframe_values.bar_wipe_duration: Start around 1 second for each bar reveal; shorten or stagger based on narration speed.
keyframe_values.bar_opacity: If using text/shape hacks, start around 60% opacity only when the chart remains readable.
keyframe_values.stagger: Offset bars by a few frames to create order, but keep total chart read time long enough for comparison.
keyframe_values.out_transition: Use a slide or fade out that does not erase data before the line is understood.

sound.rule: Use light ticks or whooshes for major chart entries only; avoid a sound on every tiny bar unless the style is intentionally rhythmic.

captions.rule: Captions should not cover axis labels or bars; suppress captions if chart text already carries the spoken data.

color.rule: Use bar colors with enough contrast against the background and each other; preserve accessible separation in grayscale where possible.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use drawbox/drawtext overlays with animated crop or enable expressions for bar growth; render chart stills to verify labels and proportions.
implementation.remotion: Create a BarChartWipe component with values, labels, colors, staggerFrames, wipeDurationFrames, and sourceCitation fields.
implementation.blender: Use rectangle planes or mesh bars with scale keyframes and text labels in an orthographic camera.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create axes with masked/shape layers, use text underscore layers or shapes as bars, rotate/scale as needed, apply Wipe Right/up-style animation, stagger layers, and compound the chart.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics shapes/text, Linear Wipe or Crop effects for bar growth, nest the chart, and use markers for narration/data beats.

common_mistakes: Animating bars without documenting the source values.
Leaving axis labels too small or hidden by captions.
Using bar lengths that do not match the data relationship.
Staggering bars so slowly that the viewer forgets the comparison.
Letting low-FPS texture make the chart hard to read.
qc: Are the data source and values known before the chart is built?
Do bar lengths accurately represent the intended comparison?
Are axis labels, category labels, and units readable or intentionally unnecessary?
Do captions avoid covering chart information?
Does animation settle long enough for the viewer to compare bars?
